accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA 7405 section 3.3.11 (amines: classification, base properties, preparation from halogenoalkanes), OCR A H432 6.2.1 and Edexcel 9CH0 Topic 18. Conjugate-acid pKa values used for the bars are ethylammonium 10.7, ammonium 9.3 and anilinium 4.6. The balanced equation uses 2NH3 and NH4Br, the conditions are excess ethanolic ammonia heated in a sealed tube, and nitrile reduction with LiAlH4 is given as the route to a pure primary amine.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the alcohol-style classification trap ((CH3)3C-NH2 refused as tertiary with 'count C on N, not on C'), writing HBr instead of NH4Br, thinking amines are neutral or are proton donors, ranking phenylamine as strong because it is large, using acid or aqueous conditions, and assuming excess haloalkane helps. The adult notes also warn against claiming tertiary amines are always strongest in water.

lab_distinct.evidence: The amine lab is built around nitrogen: a ball-and-stick N whose C-N bonds light up when classified, a lone pair that disappears into a new N-H bond, pKaH bars for ranking, and a mole-ratio slider driving a sequential-alkylation model that redistributes four product bars. flagnucphile sorts donors and acceptors generically and flaghalo covers halogenoalkane substitution and elimination; neither classifies amines, ranks basicity or models over-alkylation. The 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule emerges from feedback on the student's own choice: a wrong class names the actual carbon count on N, a wrong salt explains which way H+ moves, a wrong rank gives the inductive or delocalisation reason, and every Run at a low ratio reports the actual primary percentage with the reason the product competes. Two goals at opposite ends of the slider (90%+ primary, quaternary main) make the ratio's effect visible rather than told.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: '(CH3)3C-NH2 is tertiary, like the alcohol', 'phenylamine is strongest because it has the biggest group', and 'the bromoethane is impure' as the cause of the mixture. Each is tested directly by the task that follows, and the reveal after the task states whether the prediction held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating challenge questions cover classification (including the tert-butyl trap), salt formation, weakest base, favouring ethylamine, the nitrile route and the NH4Br by-product. Every wrong option has its own targeted fix message (thirteen in total), choices are rotated so the answer is not always first, and a streak counter rewards consecutive correct answers.

readability.evidence: Student text scores about Flesch-Kincaid 5.0 using short sentences with formulae, within the learner kid target, while still using the exact specification terms primary, secondary, tertiary, lone pair, ammonium salt, nucleophile and quaternary. Adult notes score about 8.4 and name the specification points, the conjugate-acid pKa values and the typical exam errors for parents or tutors.

no_filler.evidence: No warm-up or motivational padding: the first student sentence defines an amine, every later sentence carries a rule, an example or a reason, and the lab prompts are instructions. The content gate found no filler phrases and text overlap with other lessons stayed under the 12% limit.

mobile.evidence: Every control is a full-width button in the fl-ctl pad under the canvas, so the whole lab works by tapping with no fine dragging needed; the ratio slider can be dragged on the canvas or stepped with large minus and plus buttons. The phone sweep at Android and iPhone widths reported no overflow or clipped text, and formula labels shrink to fit their atoms.

accessibility.evidence: The canvas aria-label is updated with every spoken message, every pad button has a descriptive aria-label (for example 'Place phenylamine next, weakest first'), challenge feedback uses role status with aria-live polite, reduced motion shortens all timers, and state is shown by text and ticks as well as colour. axe passed in light and dark themes.
